subject: chunk headers, more like R's lazy formals?

messages.author: a3c668b849637905
messages.subject: chunk headers, more like R's lazy formals?
parts:
Hi,

Escaping commas in pseudo-R expressions such as keep=c(1\, 3\, 5)
feels a bit awkward and inconsistent (contrast with
background=.97;.97;1), so I was curious to know why commas (and
spaces) are so problematic in knitr's chunk options. I suspect it's
got something to do with the way those options are parsed,

https://github.com/yihui/knitr/blob/master/R/parser.R#L76

pieces = str_split(str_replace_all(pieces, fixed('\\,'), ','), '=', n = 2L)

Now, I wonder if it wouldn't be more flexible to match a list of known
chunk options (the full list is presumably available at via
opts_chunk$get()), rather than using a fixed format strsplit. In fact,
to my (probably naive) eyes, the chunk header looks a lot like the
formals() of an R function

formals(ls)
$name

$pos
-1

$envir
as.environment(pos)

$all.names
[1] FALSE

$pattern

Perhaps this analogy could be pursued further by enforcing that all
chunk parameters be valid R expressions, and ultimately used to work
around the current limitations?

Just a thought anyway!

Cheers,

baptiste

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] chunk headers, more like R's lazy formals?
parts:
Well, after experimenting with this idea for a while, I should say
this is very doable and will be a fantastic solution. All chunk
options can go to valid R code (character values should be quoted, and
R expressions like c(1, 3, 4) can be used freely). I feel lucky I did
not release the current version to CRAN today, otherwise I will surely
regret it.

However, this will introduce a nasty backward compatibility issue,
because I went astray from the very beginning, treating with chunk
options as a character string instead of function arguments.
Internally I will have to fix options like background=.97;.97;.97 to
background=c(.97,.97,.97), and fig.path=foo/bar- to
fig.path="foo/bar-".

I'm quite happy about this finding, and I believe Frank will find this
solution satisfactory as well, although the experimental feature \,
has to be dropped which will bring a little bit more manual work to
him to replace \, back to ,.

Regards,
Yihui
--
